request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the tree search, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

Type text and press Search. It lists every person in this sheet's tree whose name or an alias contains the text, ignoring case. Each line reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people, sorted by sheet id. An empty search lists everyone.

**Server:** I added `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree` (`tree.GET.yml` plus `ListTree.java`). It returns the sheets of the tree using the existing `SheetRepository.tree`, which finds the top of the parent chain and then everything below it. No data or schema changes were needed.

**Front end:** the new component is `features/summary/TreeSearch.tsx`, added to the screen in `summary.slot.tsx`. It works out each person's due-total the same way their row in the people list does, using that sheet's own rates and settings, so a result shows `n/a` exactly when the row does.
- Each search re-reads every sheet in the tree, so changes another user has made show up.
- The count (`search-count`) is blank while a search runs and is filled in once all sheets are read.
- If the tree can't be read, it shows `search-error`. No test exercises that path.
- Loading a different sheet clears the old results.

Two choices where the request left room:
- **Retired people are always included**, even when "show retired" is off. The request asks for every matching person, so I didn't apply the list's retired filter.
- **"List order" means the stored order** (the order the Up/Down buttons set), not the screen-only sort.

probe.probe_text:
I made no changes. Everything below comes from reading the code. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## Per claim (`PersonClaims.tsx`, `claims/api.ts`, `rates/api.ts`; server: `Claim`, `Dues`) | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | **status** | `ClaimStatus.moveTo`: DRAFT → OPEN; OPEN → SETTLED or PENDING; PENDING → SETTLED (approve) or OPEN (reject); DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING → VOID; DRAFT → DELETED → DRAFT (restore). `isOpen` means OPEN or PENDING. | | **number** | `ClaimNumbers.next`, given when the claim is opened. Normally `FY-`: a fiscal year taken from the claim's due-by and `fiscal-start-month`, with a sequence shared across the sheet's tree. While `period-numbering-from` is on or before today it is `-` (or `X-` when no period holds the due-by). A voided claim keeps its number. A reassigned claim gets a new one. Numbers are never reused. | | **due** | `Dues.shown` (server) and `claimDue` (front end):
1. A `settledDue` set at settlement wins outright.
2. Otherwise the figure is `statedDue` when a statement bound the claim (`isBound`; not while PENDING), else the live figure, `Dues.of` / `dueOf`. The live figure is amount × the rate in force on the claim's date, for the person's grade on that date (`gradeOn`, `RateRepository.inForce` / `rateOn`). Rates are inherited up the `parent` chain, at most `LEVELS` = 3 levels. With no rate the due is **n/a**.
3. Add the late charge: `Dues.charge` / `lateCharge`.
4. Apply `floor` last, using the floor in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). A correction has no floor. | | **rounding** | `Late.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`: HALF_UP if the claim's `roundDate` is before `policy-date` (blank means today), else HALF_EVEN. `roundDate` is the claim's own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects. | | **late charge** | Compounds: for each full 30 days past `lateFrom`, add `late-pct` in force on that boundary × (figure + charges so far), rounding each step. Only open claims that are not deferred get one; never a correction. | | **due-by** | Fixed when the claim is added (`AddClaim`, `BusinessDays.dueBy`): the claim's date plus *terms* business days, skipping weekends and holidays. Terms come from the person's own `terms`, else `terms-`, else `terms` (default 14), each as in force on the claim's date. `RefixDueBys` recomputes it, with the same stored `terms`, when a holiday is added, for claims not SETTLED, VOID or DELETED. Re-dating does not change it. | | **overdue** | `isOverdue`: open, not deferred, and `lateFrom` (due-by + `grace-` days) is before today. | | **period** | The period the claim's **due-by** falls in (not its date). | | **deferred / until** | `DeferClaim`: OPEN only, to a date after today. A deferred claim is left out of every total, is never overdue, cannot be settled or split, and a statement leaves it unbound. | | **stated** | Bound by the person's last statement. Reassign and split drop the binding. | | **late entry** | Added while its due-by period is soft-closed. | | **proofs, reminded, lines, split-from, corrects, ref, tags, void reason, batch, opened-by, lock** | Lines replace the amount with qty × unit summed (`AddClaimLine`). A `ref` may be used only once per sheet, ignoring case. A void needs a reason while the sheet has any (`VoidClaim`). `settleBatch` is set only by bulk settle. | ## Per person (`People.tsx`; server `Rollup`, `Person`) - **Which claims count.** A claim counts if it is OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED (`isCounting` / `counts`). The live rules (`countsLive` / `leftOutLive` / `liveClaims`) then drop deferred claims, and drop open claims that no statement bound if they are dated within a `Hold`, or if `isRetiredReached` (today is on or after `retiredFrom`). - **claimed**: the amounts of the live claims, leaving out claims that `corrects` another. - **due-total** (`personDue` / `Rollup`): the sum of the shown dues, skipping n/a ones, capped at `cap` (in force today). It is **n/a** when the person's grade today has no rate today and no claim is "kept". A claim is kept if it has a settled or bound figure, or a rated live figure at a grade no longer current or dated on or before today. - **excess** (`excessOf`): the uncapped total minus `cap`. - **settled / open** (`splitDues`): computed before the cap. - **overdue count / total** (`overdue`). - **aged** 0-30, 31-60 and 61+ (`agedDues`): open claims, aged by the claim's date. - **per-period due** (`personPeriodDue`): if the period is closed or soft-closed, the frozen `personTotals`. Otherwise, live claims whose due-by is in the period and whose `statusOn(c, p.to)` (from the status log) was OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. - **active** (`isActive`): has a live open claim dated in the 30 days up to today. - **backing** (`backing`): each patron's SETTLED `settledDue` over the last 90 days × their `patronShares` (100.00 split equally, rounded half-even, remainder to the first-named patron). - **cut** (`personCutTotal`, from `PoolRepository.cut`): the `pot` split by share, rounded half-even. Retired members, members with a hold in force today, and members outside their from/to dates get 0 or blank. The remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut. Nested pools are allowed, at most 3 deep. - **grade**: the one in force today (`gradeOn`). - **statement count, last due-total and date** (`TakeStatement`): records the due-total, then binds every counting claim to its **rate figure**. The late charge and floor are not bound. Taken "as of" a date, it rebuilds people, claims, rates and settings from the history tables. Only a steward may cancel a statement (`CancelStatement`). - **snapshots** (`RecordSnapshots`): each person's due-total on the day being left, written when the sheet's today changes. - **retired / retirements**, **held / holds**, **clashing** (name or alias used elsewhere in the tree), **origin**, **terms**, **contact**, **tags**. ## Sheet totals - **claimed-total.** - **due-total** and **overdue-total** (`trimmedSum`): when three or more people have a figure, drop the single highest and the single lowest. - **settled / open totals**: not trimmed. - **cut total.** - **tag totals**: a claim counts under its own tags and its person's tags. - **Summary**: per grade, the count, due and active people, excluding retired people. Per period, the due and the change from the previous period. Counts per status and per void reason. - **ALERT**: written to the audit file when a person's due-total crosses above `alert-threshold`. ## Who may do what - **Roles** (`RoleRepository.roleOf`): clerk is the default. A user is a steward while a delegation covers today; only a steward by assignment may delegate. A viewer may change nothing, and an archived sheet refuses every change (`RefuseViewer`). The as-of view (`AsOfFilter`) refuses every change. - **Permission matrix** (`Permissions`, `perm-`): open, settle, void and close default to clerk and steward; reassign and reopen default to steward. - **Steward only**: approve, reject (needs a reason), re-settle, re-date, cancel a statement, merge, transfer, archive, and voiding a SETTLED claim (within `SETTLED_DAYS` = 7 days of its settlement; this reverses its figure). - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim, or last edited it, may not settle or approve it. - **Clerk limit**: when a clerk settles a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit`, it goes to PENDING with nothing frozen. - **Proof threshold** (`requireProof`): a claim whose due is above `proof-threshold-`, else `proof-threshold`, needs at least one proof before it can be settled or approved. - **Note threshold** (`requireNote`): a claim whose due is above it cannot be opened with an empty note. - **Period cap** (`requireUnderCap`): limits how many open claims a person may have per period. ## What freezes, and when - **Settle / approve** freezes `settledDue`: the shown due, including that day's late charge and floor. **Re-settle** freezes it again as if the claim were open and unbound. - **Close or soft-close** freezes `closedTotal` and `personTotals` (`PeriodClosing.fixNow`). A hard close then refuses add, edit, lock, open, settle, approve, reject, void, defer, reassign, re-date, split, add proof, add line and delete for any claim whose due-by is in the period (`requireOpen`). Soft close freezes the figures only. Reopen unfreezes. **Auto-close**: when today changes and `grace-days` is set, open periods with to-date + grace-days before the new today are closed. - **Restore** works only on the same sheet's today the claim was deleted. A new today releases all claim locks. ## What dates decide - The **claim's date** picks the grade, rate, floor, terms, grace days, proof and note thresholds (each in force on that date), the rounding (via `roundDate`), the age buckets, active, backing, and holds and retirements. - The **due-by** picks the period, the number and overdue status. - **Today** picks the cap, the clerk limit, the late charge and the current grade. - A **blank date** means `entry-date`, else today, when adding (`AddClaim`, paste, quick-add). When editing (`ApplyClaim`) it means today. - **Retirement**: a claim dated after `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement, is refused. ## Import, paste, plans and hold - **ImportPeople**: all or nothing. A line matching a name or alias edits that person (grade from today; terms and contact only if given); otherwise it adds a person. Tree-name clashes and duplicate contacts are refused. - **PasteClaims**: all or nothing; adds DRAFTs, checked as `AddClaim` checks a claim. - **GeneratePlanClaims**: makes DRAFTs up to today, skipping dates that are refused. - **Bulk settle** is all or nothing and stamps a batch number; **bulk open** works claim by claim. - **Hold**: changes no stored data. It only removes unbound open claims from the live totals and from pool cuts. # 2. How easy this was to follow It is hard to follow. There is no single place that holds the rules. Each figure is computed twice, in Java (`Dues`, `Rollup`, `PeriodClosing`, `TakeStatement`, plus the "rate → `Dues.of` → `Dues.shown`" sequence pasted into five or more step classes) and again in TypeScript (`rates/api.ts`, `claims/api.ts`, `periods/api.ts`, `settings/api.ts`). Some rules exist only in the front end (backing, active, aged, tag totals), and the permission checks are spread across roughly a hundred one-method step classes. The comments are detailed but sometimes wrong: - `ClosePeriod`'s comment says a claim belongs to a period by its date; the code uses its due-by. - The front end describes claim numbers as "sheet-wide 1, 2, …"; the server gives `FY-`. - The holiday and due-by comments in `settings/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts` describe a calendar-day rule; the server counts business days. - Holds are described as affecting OPEN claims; the code applies them to OPEN and PENDING claims. So a new developer has to cross-check both copies and the code itself rather than trust any one description.
